Hypercasual Teardown

Object Hunt

A six-player prop hunt squeezed into fifty-second rounds. You do not choose what to become — the game hands you a chair, a toilet or an ATM and about twenty seconds. The only decision is where that object would naturally stand; once the hunt starts your camera drops to floor level and you can do nothing but watch the red cone pass by — or stop.

About one round in five or six the roulette makes you the hunter instead: thirty seconds, a glimpse of which props are in play, an edge arrow and a “someone is nearby” alert to find five fakes among real furniture. Wins advance a node bar that unlocks the next building; coins buy longer hiding time and faster feet.

Be the object that belongs there

Object Hunt never lets you pick a disguise. Each hider is turned into a random prop of the current building; the player’s skill is reading the room — where would a second ATM, a third filing cabinet or one more toilet go unnoticed?

When the roulette has chosen the hunter, the other five characters vanish in puffs of white smoke and reappear as furniture. In the recordings the player became a red dining chair, a blue office chair, a toilet, a wet-floor sign and an ATM; other hiders became a floor lamp, an arcade cabinet, a sink, a palm tree, a washing machine and a kitchen chair. There is no choice screen and no way to swap.

The countdown that follows is the only time the player acts as a hider. Dragging moves the prop across the map from a high three-quarter camera that shows the whole room and the names floating over the other disguised players. What makes a good spot shows in the outcomes: the ATM lined up beside two real ATMs was walked past at arm’s length, and the red chair parked by the dining table survived its round, while a wet-floor sign left in an empty back alley was struck at once. A toilet, by the same logic, belongs in the restroom stalls.

The game itself never rates a hiding place. No meter, outline or hint says “you blend in” — the first and only feedback is whether the hunter swings at you. That makes every round a small, private bet whose result arrives half a minute later.

Choose context, not costume: the game assigns what you are; the player only decides where it makes sense.

This is the defining decision, and it is cheap to make and expensive to get wrong: a few seconds of dragging, then thirty seconds of helpless watching. The hunter, for its part, smashes real decor as freely as disguised players — a chair, a stool, a register screen fly off when struck — so a good disguise is not one the hunter never touches, but one it has no reason to choose among many identical candidates.

Exactly how the hunter chooses what to hit — it behaves like an AI, though the game presents it as another player — is not readable from the footage. It walks a route through the rooms with its cone sweeping ahead, swings at objects along that route, sometimes ignores a hider it brushes past and sometimes lands a single fatal blow. For a rebuild this is the most consequential open rule (see D1).

One round, two cameras

A hider round is roulette, morph, countdown, hunt and verdict — about fifty seconds. Its signature device is the camera: the god’s-eye view used for hiding collapses to the prop’s own eye level the moment the hunt begins.

The round clock — what each role sees, and for how long

Player hides
RouletteArrow picks the hunter among six
Hide · 17–21 sHigh camera, drag to move, names over props, countdown top-left, “Hide!” button in the last seconds
Hunt (watched)Camera drops to the prop. Red floor cone, red silhouette through walls. No timer and no controls on screen
VerdictWin: +1 node, ≈300 · Caught: ≈half
Player hunts
RouletteArrow lands on YOU
3 · 2Glimpse of the five props
1dark

VerdictList of 5 hiders, ≈300, +1 node

Segment widths follow the on-screen timers (hide 17–21 s, hunt 30 s). The hider never sees how long the hunt will last; the hunter never waits through the hiders’ countdown — the other hiders scatter during a one-second blackout.

The two cameras divide the round into an active half and a dramatic half. During the countdown the player has full information — map, names, the other props — and full control. During the hunt the player has neither control nor a clock, but gets privileged threat information: the cone and a see-through silhouette that the hunter’s targets would not have in a real game of hide-and-seek. The design turns waiting into watching; the tension comes from knowing the hunter is two metres away and being unable to do anything about it.

Two details tighten the loop. The node bar stays on screen in both halves, so the stakes of this particular round are always visible. And the green Hide! button that appears in the last seconds lets a player who has already settled end the countdown — in the footage it is pressed at two or three seconds left, so whether it can shorten a longer remaining wait is not visible.

Thirty seconds to find five liars

As hunter the player is told a lot: which five props are in play, which way to go, when one is close. The hard part is the last metre — telling the extra chair from the real ones before the clock runs out.

MomentWhat the hunter is toldWhat stays hidden
Countdown “3, 2”All five disguises and their owners, at their starting spotsWhere each will go — the screen is black on “1”
HuntHiders left (face row), a direction (edge arrow), proximity (“someone is nearby”), the clockWhich object in range is the player; whether the arrow tracks the nearest hider
SwingHit decor shatters and flies; a hit hider drops in human form with “Попался!”The cost of a wasted swing beyond the seconds it takes
VerdictEvery hider’s fate by nameThe threshold for a hunter win (wins seen with 2 and 3 catches)

The hunter round is generous by design. The glimpse turns the search into a matching problem — “there is a palm, a sink and an arcade cabinet somewhere” — and the arrow and proximity banner shrink the search area to a room. What is left is the same reading of context the hider performed, reversed: spot the object that is one too many, or standing where it should not. Swinging is fast and decor shatters freely, so the hunter can also simply clear a room; the thirty-second clock is what keeps that brute force from being enough.

The roulette gives the role rarely. Across the two sessions the player hunted four times in about twenty-three rounds; the button above the roulette offers the role for a rewarded ad on every matchmaking screen. In the three hunter rounds checked closely the arrow landed on the player while the button was on screen, so the recordings do not show whether an ad was watched.

Getting caught pays half

A caught hider loses the node, not the session: the round still pays about half the coins, the hunter-skin card still fills, and the next roulette starts seconds later.

The capture chain is fast and legible: silhouette through a wall, the hunter rounds the corner with its cone, one swing, the player pops out of the disguise in human form, the camera rises to show the body, and the “Вас нашли” card arrives about three seconds after the blow. The same shape repeats in the starter office (swing, knockout, 150 coins).

The loss is soft. Coins are roughly halved — 150 on level 1, 152 on level 4 against 300–304 for wins — and nothing else is taken: the node bar simply does not advance, upgrades stay, and the hunter-skin card fills even after a loss (0 → 25%). The next attempt is a fresh roulette, so a failed hider round can be followed by a hunter round, as happened in the store immediately after this capture.

What the loss does not do is explain itself. Nothing on the card says what gave the player away — the open alley, the wrong object, bad luck. Combined with a hunter whose choices are not readable, the player’s lesson is “try another spot”, not “that spot was wrong because…”.

Wins buy buildings, coins buy seconds

Two currencies run in parallel. Round wins — as hider or hunter — fill a node bar that unlocks the next building. Coins from every round buy three upgrades whose price rises by $100 per level.

LevelBuildingWins neededUnlock card offers
1Starter office (no name shown): desks, brick pillars, small tiled washroom2—
2Дом · House: living room with Christmas tree and arcade cabinet, kitchen, bathroom, garage with a pickup4Bin, coat stand, toilet
3Офис · Office: whiteboards, filing cabinets, checkerboard restroom, reception, pool table4Desk fan, foosball table, office chair
4Магазин · Store: aisles, checkout, ATMs, back alley with dumpsters4 (bar)Hot-dog counter, fridge, ice-cream freezer
5+Not reached in the recordings; the store page promises “multiple environments”.

A hunter win advances the bar exactly like a hider win — in both sessions a hunter round filled the last node of a building. A loss leaves it untouched. Each completed building raises a “Разблокирован новый уровень!” card with the map’s name and three “special objects” that can be unlocked for an ad, then the lobby switches to the new building.

$100 × levelPrice of the next level of any upgrade: $100 at level 1 up to $600 at level 6 (all seen on cards)
17 s → 21 sHide countdown at Time level 1, and later with Time at level 4 or above. The step per level is not established.
30 sHunter clock in every checked hunt, after several Time upgrades — Time does not lengthen the hunt
≈300 / ≈150Coins per win / per loss, creeping from 300 to 304 over two sessions

Time lengthens the hiding countdown, Speed makes the character and prop move faster (its size is not measured), and Offline earnings (“Заработок не в сети”) promises coins while the game is closed — no payout appears in either recording. A purchase deducts at once: 300 coins became 0 when Offline earnings went from level 3 to 4. A red “УЛУЧШИТЬ” tag marks one card at a time, apparently the next affordable or recommended one. Early on, one round buys one upgrade; from level 4 prices exceed a win, so upgrades slow to one every couple of rounds while the building nodes keep moving.

A third track runs after every round, won or lost: a “НОВЫЙ ВЕДУЩИЙ!” (new hunter) card fills by a percentage toward a hunter skin — a faceless man in a suit, a white goose, a clown with a cleaver, a figure in a hazmat suit. Fills of 25 to 50 points per round were seen. At 100% the skin is claimed by watching an ad; the alternative is a small link literally reading “Промах” (Miss), the localisation of a Skip button.

An ad offer on every exit

The rounds themselves are free of offers. Everything between two rounds is a chain of cards, and nearly every card has a rewarded-ad button with a delayed plain exit.

Verdict cardwin / Вас нашли→ Level unlockspecial objects · ad→ Golden chestafter a hunt · ОТКРЫТЬ · ad→ Coins ×2 / ×3ДУБЛЬ / ТРИЖДЫ · ad · СОБРАТЬ after ~2 s→ New hunter %ПОЛУЧИТЬ · ad · Промах→ Lobbyupgrades · ADS-off · tap to start→ RouletteСтаньте ВЕДУЩИМ · ad

Five rewarded-ad offers appear in the footage: doubling or tripling the round’s coins (“ДУБЛЬ ×2”, “ТРИЖДЫ ×3”), opening the golden chest found during a hunt, unlocking a building’s special props, claiming a finished hunter skin, and becoming the hunter. On each, the plain exit — “СОБРАТЬ”, “Нет, спасибо”, “Промах” — is smaller and shows up about two seconds after the ad button. A crossed-out “ADS” button in the lobby sells ad removal (Remove Ads, $2.99 on the US App Store).

The settings screen is minimal: one vibration toggle, a feedback mail button and the privacy policy, under a “Publish with kwalee” banner. There is no sound or music control; in one recording the narrator could not find any game sound at all. Interstitial ads may exist but are not visible in edited footage.

For the analysis this matters in two ways. The between-round chain costs two to five taps and ten to twenty seconds (13 s from a capture to the next roulette, 18 s after a win that unlocked a building), a large share of a fifty-second loop. And three things that shape play — the hunter role, the coin multiplier and the special props — are reached most directly through ads; a web adaptation without ads has to give them other routes.

Product, audience and reception

A long-running Kwalee title from 2021 that still ships updates, sold as the “ultimate prop hunt” and played in short sessions.

Offer. Free on iOS and Android with ads; the only in-app purchases listed on the US App Store are ad removal ($2.99, discounted $1.99). Rated 13+ on the App Store (cartoon violence, mild horror) and Everyone 10+ on Google Play. 252.6 MB on iOS, sixteen languages including Russian — the language of both recordings. The store subtitle is “Stay hidden”; the Google Play text calls it “the ultimate prop hunt game where classic hide-and-seek meets hilarious disguises” and lists props, an “Epic Hunter Mode”, unlockable skins and multiple environments.

History. The App Store version history runs from 1.0.7 (16 April 2021) to 1.5.6 (21 July 2026), with recent notes reading only “Bug fixes and improvements”; Google Play shows an update on 19 August 2026. The current Google Play description mentions a “Meccha Madness” skin and prop set that does not appear in the recordings, so the live build has content beyond what was observed. No developer posts, patch notes or interviews about the game’s design were found.

Audience. The store copy addresses casual players who know prop hunt from PC and Roblox culture; the hunter in both recordings is a pink pig with a plank, an obvious nod to Roblox’s Piggy. The observed game demands little dexterity and no reading beyond a few UI words — spatial judgement about rooms and furniture, and patience through thirty seconds of watching — which fits a young mobile audience and the store’s “quick gaming sessions” promise.

Reception snapshot · looked up 8 Oct 2026

  • App Store (US): 4.6 / 5 from about 81K ratings — listing.
  • Google Play (US, English): 4.3 / 5 from 306K reviews, 10M+ downloads — listing.
  • Steam: not on Steam.
  • Critics: no Metacritic or OpenCritic page and no published review were found; only player-guide pages exist.

Reading. Large player samples on both stores are clearly positive, and the lower Google Play score comes from a much larger review sample. These are store ratings over five years of updates, not a measure of the build in the footage, of retention or of revenue; the absence of critical coverage is normal for a mobile hypercasual title.

What to take from it

  1. Assign the costume, leave the context.A random prop removes the “best disguise” meta and turns every round into a fresh reading of the room — the one decision that matters is where.
  2. Drop the camera when control ends.Switching the hider to the prop’s eye level, with a cone and a see-through silhouette, turns thirty seconds without input into the tensest part of the round.
  3. Give the seeker a glimpse, not an answer.Seeing the five disguises, then an arrow and a proximity alert, makes hunting a matching puzzle solvable in thirty seconds.
  4. Never pay zero.Half coins on a loss plus a skin bar that fills anyway keep a failed round from feeling wasted, while only wins move the building forward.
  5. One bar for two roles.Hider wins and hunter wins advance the same node bar, so the rare hunter round is a bonus, not a detour.
Weak spots a rebuild should fix: captures do not explain themselves; the hunter’s targeting is opaque; the hunter role is rationed by luck or an ad; ten seconds of offer cards sit between fifty-second rounds; and there is no audio control.

Build layer

Everything a builder needs to make the complete mobile web adaptation for bug.games from this one file: the short prompt, rules with their evidence, the target game, design space, platform plan and acceptance cases. Status tags: Observed Inferred Designed Unknown External.

How to read this file

  1. Parse the HTML structurally (an HTML parser, not line deletion). Strip data:image payloads from your text view but keep captions, alt text, tables and the <details> blocks — their text is part of the specification.
  2. Extract every <img> inside a figure to your working directory under its figure id and open the files with an image tool. Check that every ID in the evidence index exists, decodes and shows what its caption says.
  3. Compare the three reference episodes against their frames: EP-01 (hider survives), EP-02 (hider caught) and EP-03 (player hunts).
  4. Then follow the Build prompt. Rules R1–R20 and core statements C1–C4 are authoritative for the source; everything marked Designed is yours to revise through play-testing, as long as the core statements still hold.

Build prompt

Build "Blend & Bonk" (working title — do not use the Object Hunt name, Kwalee branding, the pig hunter's look, Roblox Piggy or any source art), the complete mobile web adaptation of Object Hunt specified in this HTML, delivered as ONE portable HTML file for bug.games. Fantasy: six characters, one hunter, five hiders who become furniture. Keep the source's decisions exactly (#core-statements C1–C4): a hider is handed a random prop and a short countdown to put it where such an object naturally belongs; when the hunt starts the camera drops to the prop's eye level and the player can only watch the hunter's red cone and see-through silhouette come closer. The hunter gets 30 seconds, a glimpse of the five disguises, an edge arrow and a "someone is nearby" alert to find the fakes among real furniture. Wins of either role fill one node bar that unlocks the next building; every round pays coins (a loss about half) for Time, Speed and Offline-earnings upgrades. New session form: ~50-second rounds in a portrait phone browser, one thumb (drag to move), verdict → next roulette in one tap. Deliver the whole game in #complete-game: all six buildings and the endless remix cycle after them, both roles with the visible hunter-chance meter, honest AI opponents, special props, the golden chest, the hunter wardrobe, offline earnings, save/continue, pause, Settings (English/Русский, separate Music and Sound-effects sliders), credits, and the bug.games plan with its optional Extra in #bug-games. Design what #design-space leaves open — above all the AI hunter's suspicion model (D1) and the AI hiders' spot choice (D2) — so that a careful placement visibly beats a careless one and every capture can be explained. Follow #art-direction, #assets and #audio; design the first 20 minutes from #roblox-hooks and bridge rows B12–B17. EP-01, EP-02 and EP-03 are the fidelity references. Aim higher than the original in art, readability and sound. Play-test on a 390×844 touch viewport with real touches, run #acceptance, and fix what fails — all in this build. A demo, one building or a promise to finish later is not completion. Report your design decisions and the actual test coverage.

Launch instruction for the receiving agent: “Build the complete web game from this teardown. First parse the whole HTML, including its Build layer, without loading base64 into your text context. Extract the embedded evidence into your working directory and inspect it with an image tool; list any missing required figure IDs. Then follow the in-document Build prompt.”

Scope, sources and versions

Target: a mobile web adaptation (not a faithful reconstruction) of Object Hunt for bug.games, playable offline as one HTML file, mobile-first in a portrait browser window. Source model: two Russian-localised recordings of the current-era mobile game, plus store pages. Source behaviour and designed behaviour are kept apart below.

Core statements

  • C1 · Placement is the hider’s decision. The hider receives a random prop and a countdown (17–21 s); moving it into a spot where that object belongs — beside its duplicates or in its room — is the only choice that affects survival, because during the hunt the hider has no control (EP-01, EP-02). Observed + Inferred causality
  • C2 · The hunt is elimination under a clock. The hunter sees which five props are in play, then has 30 s with a direction arrow and a proximity alert; each swing either shatters decor or catches a hider, and only catches change the face row and the verdict (EP-03). Observed
  • C3 · Every round pays; only wins advance. Win ≈300 coins and one node; caught ≈half the coins and no node; nodes unlock the next building (2 wins on level 1, 4 later). Hider and hunter wins count the same. Observed
  • C4 · Coins buy an edge for the next round. Time (longer hide countdown), Speed (faster movement), Offline earnings; the next level costs $100 × current level. Observed prices effect sizes

Principles (how this game works)

  • Situations come from a random prop meeting a fixed room. Good rooms offer duplicates and themed corners; the variety of rounds comes from the pairing, not from new rules. Inferred
  • Teaching is wordless: one Russian verb per phase (Hide!, Search!), the cone and the silhouette. No tutorial was observed (V2 started at level 1 without one). Observed
  • Escalation is mostly spatial — bigger buildings with more rooms (store plus alley) and more nodes — while Time and Speed upgrades soften it. Hunter difficulty growth is not visible. Inferred
  • Reward is steady and small: coins every round, a node per win, a building every 2–4 wins, a skin card every few rounds. Nothing is lost permanently. Observed

Art direction and signals

Designed Keep the toy-box low-poly interiors and bright flat colours that make furniture silhouettes instantly readable, but with an original cast: a new comic hunter (not a pig in green, not any known horror character) and original skin ideas. Camera: hide phase at a high 3/4 angle showing the whole room above the thumb; hunt-as-hider at ~1 m behind the prop, never covered by the HUD; hunt-as-hunter following from above with the next room visible. HUD top band only: timer left, node bar centre, face row (hunter), pause right. At the moment of decision the room, the prop and the threat outrank effects.

SignalFunctionSource figureTarget treatment
“YOU” tagOwner of the propfig-morphBigger, outlined, fades during the hunt view
CountdownDecision pressurefig-hide-startRing timer, last 5 s pulse + tick
Red coneWhere the hunter looksfig-pov-houseKeep; brighter edge when it touches the player
See-through silhouetteWhere the hunter isfig-pov-pillar, fig-alley-silhouetteKeep; red, never confused with props

Audio brief

Source audio not heard Both recordings carry narration and creator music; V2’s narrator says the game had no sound. Everything here is Designed.

  • Events (SFX bus): roulette tick + stop thunk; hunter reveal (comic villain sting); morph poof; prop drag scrape loop; last-5-seconds tick; Hide! lock click; hunter footsteps scaled by distance; telegraph “huh?”; swing whoosh; decor shatter (wood/glass variants); capture bonk + squeak; catch “Gotcha!” chime; chest found; coin tally; node pop; building unlock fanfare; skin unlock sparkle; UI taps.
  • Music (music bus): lobby — bouncy, light percussion; hide — quick pizzicato with a ticking pulse; hunt-as-hider — sparse sneaking bass that thickens as footsteps approach; hunt-as-hunter — playful chase drums; verdict stings (win / caught) as short separate cues.
  • Audio starts after the first gesture; the game is fully understandable with both sliders at 0.

Settings: language and audio

Designed A gear in the lobby and on the pause screen opens Settings: Language English / Русский switching every player-facing string at once (lobby, roulette, prop names, coach marks, timers, verdicts and cause labels, unlock and skin cards, wardrobe, errors, Extra states); Music slider 0–100% and Sound effects slider 0–100% on independent gain buses with visible values and touch-draggable thumbs; Vibration toggle where supported. Language and both levels are device preferences in their own storage key, restored after reload; 0% is silent. The first round is never blocked by Settings.

Roblox analogs and first-minutes hooks

Searched the company knowledge base (Bloom Brain, search_kb, 2026-10-08) with: “prop hunt hide and seek disguise as object furniture morph blend in seeker hunter roblox”; “hide and seek hider seeker round timer countdown tagged caught first time user experience FTUE roblox”; “Piggy horror chase bat knock out survive round roblox escape killer asymmetric”; “camouflage hide in plain sight become a prop disguise transform into object seekers find hiders hide and seek extreme”; “round-based murderer sheriff innocent random role selection roulette lobby who is the killer reveal round result screen”; “Flee the Facility beast hide survivors computers freeze pods round lobby beast chance”; “death recap killcam show why you died cause of failure replay readable loss near miss heartbeat proximity warning tension”; “first round easy win guaranteed first success onboarding bots fill lobby short round 30 seconds instant replay next round button”. The base has no Roblox prop-hunt page; the accepted donors each solve one named problem.

ProblemAnalog technique (KB path, date)Transfer hereRisk to coreHypothesis and test

H2 · “I never get to be the hunter” (source: luck or an ad)kevin game — Merit Role Queue: the chance to become murderer climbs with rounds played and is shown as a percentage (24% after ~20 min). artifacts/pages/kevin-game-technical-teardown.md, 2026-09-02B8, D12: “Hunter chance” meter on the matchmaking screen, guaranteed at 100%Hunter rounds too frequent dilute hidingEvery player hunts by round ~4 and then every 4–5 rounds; players can say when their next hunt is

H4 · Long pause between short roundsNatural Disaster Survival — death is quiet and fast, survivors are listed by name, a new round follows within a minute. artifacts/pages/natural-disaster-survival-teardown.md, 2026-08-14B14: keep the named fate list, drop the offer chain; one tap to the next rouletteLess time to notice the metaMedian time from verdict to next roulette ≤4 s

bug.games plan

Designed The complete game above is the free base and works without the platform. Inside bug.games, import /sdk/bloomplay.js only when embedded (window.parent !== window), initialise it, and distinguish “no platform” from an initialisation error; check the current sdk_docs before building. Call gameplayStart() when a round’s countdown begins and gameplayStop() on the verdict, pause and leaving; report moments with progress.moment(name). Do not duplicate the platform’s automatic page-view and gameplay events. No ads, no coin top-ups, no income claims.

Provenance, method and limits
  • Packet: Gemini Analyses/Object Hunt/2026-10-08T16-21-17-277Z-3464af67 (extension 0.5.2). Integrity check passed (73 files). Both reports and their saved requests were read in full; the reports served as locators only.
  • All 24 packet frames were opened; 9 showed the expected state, 8 partially, 7 a different or empty state (for example unlock cards captured before they rendered). Contradictions were settled from frames: level 1 needs 2 wins (not 3); hunter rounds credit hiders as 3 catches where a report counted a chest as a catch; a “Hide!” button exists near the end of the countdown; upgrade prices follow $100 × level.
  • Clips: nine bounded YouTube excerpts acquired with the skill’s helper (1080p), reviewed as 1–2 fps contact sheets and decoded stills; one excerpt failed (audio-only). Both videos are edited, so durations between non-adjacent states are approximate and some intervals are cut.
  • Audio: not listened to with an audio-capable tool. Narration and creator music cover both tracks; source sound design is unverified.
  • Not established: AI hunter targeting; effect of pressing Hide!; Speed and Offline-earnings values; hunter win threshold; buildings beyond the Store; skin increment rule; whether opponents are real players; interstitial ads.
